slot.brief: Give a diene/trisubstituted alkene in the figure; ozonolysis under reductive workup — ask which carbonyl fragments form, including how many moles of a specific product per mole.

stem: One mole of the diene shown undergoes reductive ozonolysis. Which carbonyl products, and in what amounts, are formed?

verdicts.working: Cleavage of both C=C bonds gives one acetone from each end carbon bearing two methyl groups, and the two inner carbons form one ethanedial molecule. Thus the amounts are 2 mol acetone and 1 mol ethanedial.

working:
Cleavage of both C=C bonds gives $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C=O}$ from each end carbon with no H.
The two inner carbons remain joined, giving $\text{OHC–CHO}$.
Products per mole of diene: $2$ mol acetone and $1$ mol ethanedial.

Independent check: Cleavage of both C=C bonds gives one acetone from each end carbon bearing two methyl groups, and the two inner carbons form one ethanedial molecule. Thus the amounts are 2 mol acetone and 1 mol ethanedial.
solution: Reductive ozonolysis cleaves both $C=C$ bonds to form carbonyl groups at each alkene carbon. The two terminal carbons each give acetone, while the joined inner carbons give ethanedial: $2$ mol acetone and $1$ mol ethanedial.
